supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS connections are attributable to cmupdate.exe running from Ben Carter's user-writable AppData path, and the proxy identifies the destination as update.chartmate-imaging.net. The supplied inventory instead lists the approved updater at C:\Program Files\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe and the update host as update.chartmate-imaging.com, so the observed process and destination do not match the approved entries.

A domain credential validation for omar.haddad names WS-BCARTER-01 as the source workstation, and WS-OHADDAD-01 records a successful network logon for omar.haddad from that workstation. This is inconsistent with the supplied practice that remote administration is performed only from WS-OHADDAD-01.
Dropbox.exe ran on WS-BCARTER-01. The supplied inventory says no file-sharing or cloud-storage services other than the listed approved services are approved.
Explorer set the user's Internet Settings ProxyEnable value to 0 during the review window.

A file named installer-70930.exe was created in Ben Carter's Downloads folder. The available record identifies RuntimeBroker.exe as the creating process but does not identify the file's source or contents.

There was also a successful network logon for ben.carter on WS-BCARTER-01 sourced from WS-OHADDAD-01, consistent with the stated direction of authorized remote administration; this does not explain the separate omar.haddad authentication originating from WS-BCARTER-01.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnels, but the available evidence does not provide complete encrypted payload contents or the updater's downloaded response content.
The file-creation record for installer-70930.exe provides no hash, signature, download source, or execution evidence.
The supplied records do not establish whether the observed software, account use, or proxy setting change was authorized.
claims_not_established: That cmupdate.exe is definitively malicious, rather than an unlisted or misconfigured ChartMate installation.
That installer-70930.exe was downloaded from a particular site or executed.
That Dropbox transferred files or data out of the organization.
Who initiated the omar.haddad authentication from WS-BCARTER-01, or whether the credentials were compromised.
Whether any of the observed activity resulted in data theft, persistence, or other impact.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect cmupdate.exe metadata, hash, signature, installation history, and endpoint telemetry; verify the observed host and executable with ChartMate or the software owner.
Retrieve proxy and DNS details for update.chartmate-imaging.net, including available TLS inspection, certificate, and response data.
Determine the source, hash, signature, and subsequent execution history of installer-70930.exe.
Review Dropbox network, synchronization, and file-access records to determine whether data was transferred.
Correlate WS-BCARTER-01, WS-OHADDAD-01, and domain-controller authentication records with administrator activity and confirm whether omar.haddad credentials were used legitimately.
Identify the process or user responsible for changing ProxyEnable and confirm whether the change was authorized.
